fields.description:
## Summary

Production cutover must preserve already-issued integration identities, reconcile Salesforce ↔ CMS mappings deliberately, and enable the new sender in controlled stages.

## Data principle

Do **not** bulk-regenerate or “clean up” External Deal IDs merely because current source fields/formulas would produce a different value.

Once an External Deal ID has been used as an activated/integration identity, preserve it unless a specific Salesforce/CMS reconciliation explicitly requires a correction.

Partial Sandbox records are test data; no automated legacy-backfill feature is required solely to make those records conform.

## Work Required

### 1. Pre-test / pre-cutover readiness

* Identify existing Deals used for UAT that need minimal manual setup to enter the new lifecycle safely (for example First Activated Date or lifecycle Dates on a test record).
* Prefer creating fresh Deals through the target process where practical.
* If existing production Deals require First Activated to prevent post-activation fields being treated as editable, prepare a **one-time data-fix list** before enabling lifecycle enforcement. This is migration/cutover work, not permanent automation.
* Do not modify historical External Deal IDs unless specifically approved.

### 2. Production Salesforce ↔ CMS identity map

With Strah/WagerTech:

* build/confirm Salesforce External Deal ID ↔ CMS row map;
* identify real mismatches;
* decide case-by-case whether Salesforce or CMS needs correction/retirement before the first push;
* confirm SLC matching continues by External Deal ID.

### 3. Credentials/config

* production key entered only through approved credential storage.
* verify production Named Credential URL.
* deploy with sending **off**.
* safe initial config:

    * Enabled = false;
    * Include Test Records = false;
    * Include Links = false until Link staging is approved.
    
* never expose secrets in Jira/test evidence.

### 4. Single outbound path check

* Queueable WAGR-454 is the intended outbound sender.
* Verify whether any external subscriber is actually consuming Deal CDC.
* Existing External Service/CDC metadata must not create a duplicate production send path.
* If a real CDC consumer exists, document/resolve it before enabling the new sender.

### 5. Controlled enablement

* smoke test one approved Deal;
* verify Salesforce + CMS result;
* enable Deal sending;
* run controlled re-sync/full sync;
* enable Affiliate Links only after WAGR-459/WAGR-499/contract dependencies are ready.

### 6. Hypercare

* verify counts and representative fields in CMS;
* confirm no `active_makeup_conflict` from identity mismatches;
* WagerTech completes any manual Operator/Partner CMS mappings;
* agree who monitors Salesforce/CMS failure alerts.

## Done When

* Every eligible production Deal is Synced or has an agreed remediation reason.
* No unintended External Deal ID regeneration occurred.
* No duplicate outbound sender is active.
* No `active_makeup_conflict` is caused by unreviewed identity mismatches.
* WagerTech confirms CMS values and SLC matching are correct.

## Dependencies

* WAGR-458 staging Deal verification.
* WAGR-459 staging Affiliate Link verification if Links go live.
* WAGR-445 credential work.
* Data Migration epic where applicable.
* WAGR-499 before production Links.
* CMS-side SLC reprocess capability required for production support.
